ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a filtering system, with input X(t) on the left and output Y(t) on the right. The filter box is labeled with the magnitude-squared response |H(f)|^2; its curve is triangular, nonzero on the frequency axis from -10 kHz to +10 kHz, and reaches the peak value 1 at f=0. Reasoning: The two-sided power spectral density of the input white noise is S_X(f)=1×10^-10 W/Hz. The output power spectral density is S_Y(f)=S_X(f)|H(f)|^2. The output power equals the integral over all frequencies: P_Y = ∫ S_Y(f) df = S_X × ∫ |H(f)|^2 df. The area of |H(f)|^2 in the figure is the area of a triangle, with base 20 kHz = 20000 Hz and height 1, so the area = (1/2)×20000×1 = 10000 Hz. Therefore P_Y = 1×10^-10 × 10000 = 1×10^-6 W.
